messages:
Maya: Ran the tenant failover simulation for the EU + NA active/active mix this morning. Summary in the run artifact: https://artifacts.internal/runs/2024-06-15/tenant-failover-42 — key takeaways below.

deploy-bot: CI job completed: failover-sim/tenant-42 — logs: https://ci.internal/builds/9876

Maya: TL;DR — 1) failovers triggered correctly for 98% of requests, 2) a class of long-tail sessions (~2%) experienced KV cache miss storms after regional swap, 3) one tenant with residency=EU fell back to NA for a short window due to our fallback policy.

James: Can you paste the small log snippet for the residency breach? Want to understand whether it was a routing decision or a stale hint.

Maya: Sure — snippet:
```
2024-06-15T08:12:01Z Router: route_decision tenant=acme-eu preferred_region=eu-west-1 fallback=na-east-1 reason=quota_exhausted
2024-06-15T08:12:01Z ResidencyGuard: tenant_policy=EU_ONLY allow_fallback=false override=false
2024-06-15T08:12:02Z Router: applied_policy=soft_fallback (consent_check=timeout)
```

Olga: Hmm the ResidencyGuard shows allow_fallback=false but Router applied soft_fallback because consent_check timed out. That implies our consent check RPC latency caused the route to pick fallback even though policy forbids it.

Liam: Did the consent RPC call go to the control plane region? We saw higher p99 there during the sim because we deliberately throttled the control-plane endpoint.

Maya: Yes — in the simulation we throttled control-plane to emulate partial control-plane outage. That reproduced a realistic failure mode: consent-check timeout => soft fallback.

James: That's a big deal for EU_ONLY tenants. Two options: 1) change Router to treat consent-check timeouts as hard-fail (reject) when tenant_policy=EU_ONLY, 2) add a cached consent token in the edge proxy with short TTL so route decision doesn't always need control-plane call.

Olga: Option 2 reduces blast radius but adds cache invalidation complexity. We saw cache-storms earlier when many sessions tried to warm KV after swap.

sre-bot: Observed metric spike: kv-miss-rate +400% in eu-west-1 after swap window 08:12—08:18Z. Related alerts: kv-backpressure triggered.

Liam: We should also consider read-proxy behavior: reads can be allowed from NA for non-sensitive data if consent is not required, but routing must strictly avoid writes. The simulation showed writes were correctly blocked but some ephemeral reads were misclassified due to header stripping in the edge.

Maya: Action items proposal (short):
- run another sim with control-plane throttled but consent cache enabled at edge (TTL=30s) to see if cache prevents routing to NA.
- implement change: Router treats consent RPC timeout as NO_CONSENT for EU_ONLY tenants (reject or 503) behind a configurable flag.
- add a synthetic canary test that asserts no residency breaches for EU_ONLY in failover runs.
- update runbook with clear guidance: if control-plane consensus lost, prefer rejecting requests for EU_ONLY over failing open.

James: +1 to canary test and runbook. For the consent-cache, can we scope it to metadata-only keys (no PII) to avoid storing residency-affecting data at edge? @Olga thoughts.

Olga: Yes, store a short-lived consent marker only (consent=true/false/timestamp). No tenant data. That keeps KMS/HSM out of the cache path.

sre-bot: Scheduled simulated run: failover-sim/tenant-42-rerun at 2024-06-18T09:00Z. Will post results automatically.

deploy-bot: Patch branch for Router timeout handling created: https://git.internal/redwood/routers/pulls/224 — experimental flag router.fail_on_consent_timeout

Liam: Next meeting? Quick sync Wed 09:30 to decide whether to roll the flag to canary.

Maya: Thanks all. I'll kick off the consent-cache rerun and paste results in this thread. For the runbook change I'll draft a short PR and request reviews from @James and @Olga. :thumbsup:
